name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,277

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: After time this would result in repetitive spasm of abnormal stress

indicators.text: After time this would result in
indicators.note: the answer is what is left when you take a longer phrase and remove the letter that would have to be put in front of it

blocks.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch; repeat it and you have tic-tic
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A medical note on a repeated twitch brought on by strain, appearing after some delay.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: put T in front of ICTIC and you get TIC-TIC, a repeated spasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Ictus is the metrical beat in verse and also a medical seizure; the adjective formed from that noun describes such emphasis.

clue.text: They’ll spoil cool sauce containing bases from our beurre noir

indicators.note: in a down clue the base of each word is its bottom, so its final letter is taken
the sauce word holds the selected letters inside it

blocks.note: in means fashionable, cool
jus is a thin meat-juice sauce
last letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A cookery warning that a cold sauce will be ruined by browned butter.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who injure something damage or harm it, much as spoilers ruin a thing.

clue.text: Preparation of bamboo sap: try one covered with salt

indicators.note: being covered means wrapped by the outer word, so the attempt and the one sit inside it

blocks.note: a salt and a tar are both old sailors
to have a bash is to have a try
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A recipe tip: taste a bamboo-sap concoction after it has been sprinkled with salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabashir is a hard siliceous substance found in bamboo joints, used medicinally in the East.

clue.text: Chapter four’s ending with morals about most unusual area of a learner’s anthology

indicators.note: the ending of the number word is its final letter
unusual signals the letters of the preceding word come out in an odd order
the morals word goes around the rearranged group

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for chapter
final letter of four
having morals is being ethical
taken as written, then rearranged
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A moral fable whose fourth chapter ends with a strange passage in a student's reader.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged group with the area letter goes in after the first letter of the morals word; a chrestomathy is a reader of selected passages.
explanation.definitionFit: A chrestomathy is a collection of selected passages compiled for students learning a language.

clue.text: Width in top seats, best condition for flyer from Prestwick

indicators.note: in places the width letter inside the seating word

blocks.note: the gods are the highest balcony seats in a theatre
W is the abbreviation for width
in the pink means in the best of health

explanation.surface: An airline reviewer praises roomy first-class seats on a plane leaving Prestwick airport.
explanation.walkthrough: Prestwick is in Ayrshire, Scotland, so the flyer is a Scottish bird; the surface wants it to be a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Scots dialect name for the goldfinch, a small songbird of Scottish hedgerows.

clue.text: Good stuff to use for writing case

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
the liquid a pen writes with

explanation.surface: Recommending quality materials for writing up a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: A case is slang for an odd or eccentric person, not a legal matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gink is old slang for a fellow, especially a peculiar one, like calling someone a real character.

clue.text: Edges of garish long scarf hemmed with strange thin seam

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters
something hemmed is bordered all round, so the oddity word surrounds what comes before

blocks.note: first and last letters of garish
a boa is a long feathery scarf
weird means strange

explanation.surface: A dressmaker's note: a loud scarf finished off with an odd narrow seam.
explanation.walkthrough: Seam here is a geological layer, not a line of stitching as the sewing surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: In mining, this is a narrow vein of clay cutting across a lode, i.e. a thin geological layer.

clue.text: Wayward discontent saved in Redeemer’s return I believe

definitions.note: the definition is the creed of the person, who is the answer

indicators.note: wayward means straying from the proper course, so the following letters wander out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lapsed believer's restlessness is redeemed by faith in Christ coming again.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of this sect hold that Christ will physically come to earth once more, which is their central belief.

clue.text: Flock in turn express satisfaction during appeal

indicators.note: turned round means the purring word is read in the opposite direction
during places one item inside the time span of the other, so the turned word goes inside

blocks.note: it is sex appeal
a contented cat purrs

explanation.surface: A crowd taking turns to show contentment while making a plea.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds or animals said to irrupt suddenly migrate in large numbers into a new area, arriving as a mass.

clue.text: Massages as protection for joints with excision at the centre

indicators.note: an excision is a cutting out, here of the middle letters of the padding word

blocks.note: pads strapped over the knees

explanation.surface: A physiotherapist's rub-down acting like padding for sore joints after surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The two central letters, E and P, are cut from the eight-letter pads.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead is to work and press muscles with the hands, which is what a masseur does.

clue.text: Inject privates with iodine drug to produce sweating

blocks.note: a jab is an injection
OR stands for other ranks, i.e. private soldiers
and means together with
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: An army medic injects soldiers with iodine, making them sweat.
explanation.walkthrough: Privates looks like a body part but means private soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the dried leaflet of a South American shrub, used medically as a diaphoretic to induce perspiration.

clue.text: Bent, discarded and black in the middle

definitions.note: discarded marks the word as obsolete

indicators.note: in places the colour letter inside the word for the middle

blocks.note: the core is the centre
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: Something warped, thrown away and blackened at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenser used this old word meaning crooked or curved, now no longer in use.

clue.text: Exclude middle third from an irregular protective coating

indicators.note: the central three of nine letters are to be left out

blocks.note: a reservist is a part-time soldier rather than a regular

explanation.surface: Instructions to strip part of an uneven protective layer.
explanation.walkthrough: Irregular wants to be an anagram signal, but here it is a noun, a non-regular soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: In dyeing and etching, a substance applied to stop dye or acid reaching the covered parts is called this.

clue.text: Layer in firm container for beans or beetroot, say

indicators.note: in puts the layer inside the company abbreviation

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
a hen lays eggs
beans grow in a pod

explanation.surface: Packing advice: put a layer of beans or beetroot in a sturdy box.
explanation.walkthrough: Layer is a hen, not a stratum.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetroot belongs to the goosefoot family of plants, whose members are given this name; it is one example.

clue.text: Perhaps Belafonte with lowered head and level height raised beat’s irregularity

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means written upwards, so the aiming and height pair runs backwards

blocks.note: Harry Belafonte, the calypso singer; his first letter is moved lower down the word
to level a gun is to aim it
HT is the abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: Harry Belafonte, head bowed, with a calypso rhythm whose beat rises unevenly.
explanation.walkthrough: HARRY has its H dropped three places to give ARRHY.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical term means an irregular heartbeat, with the rhythm of the heart disturbed.

clue.text: Alien, horror edited with extra hour for streaming?

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective for a runny nose

indicators.note: an edited text is reworked, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hour, added as an extra letter

explanation.surface: A sci-fi film recut with an extra hour, ready for online streaming.
explanation.walkthrough: Streaming suggests online video; the question mark flags the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinorrhoea is the medical term for a runny nose, so a nose that is streaming fits this adjective.

clue.text: Extremely anti a truck, actively opposing inward traffic?

indicators.note: only the extremities of the word anti are kept
actively suggests lively movement, so the letters are shifted around

blocks.note: first and last letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A protester strongly against lorries, campaigning to block traffic coming into town.
explanation.walkthrough: Inward traffic means imports, not lorries.
explanation.definitionFit: An autarkic economy is self-sufficient, aiming to do without imports from other nations.

clue.text: Number orfe among yield mostly producing shiny-scaled fish

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
among puts the first pair inside the shortened yield word

blocks.note: a gain is a yield or profit
NO is the abbreviation for number
the orfe is a fish also called the ide

explanation.surface: A fish farmer counts orfe among the harvest, mostly glittering specimens.
explanation.definitionFit: This order of fish, including sturgeon and gars, has hard enamelled ganoid scales that glisten.

clue.text: Literary Greek king engaged in race with very old country outside Europe

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
at as in at work, busy with
to hare is to run fast
V is the abbreviation for very
O is the abbreviation for old
the United States, an American country

explanation.surface: A king joins a race with an ancient nation from beyond Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Engaged in and race look like a container; they are two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the purified formal style of modern Greek, modelled on the ancient language and used in writing.

clue.text: To accommodate a husband, wife rebuffed speculation

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so the whole string runs the other way

blocks.note: to fit in is to accommodate
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife refuses to make room for her husband amid gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypothetical question about possible outcomes is called this, a guess about something imagined.

clue.text: Again taking part, despite rumours

indicators.note: the answer takes only part of the phrase that follows

blocks.note: the letters sit across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone joins in once more in spite of the gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin word, used in English for a repeated action, means a second time or once more.

clue.text: Sailing the yacht as a cutter

indicators.note: a sailing boat moves about, so these letters drift into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Taking the yacht out to sail as though it were a cutter.
explanation.walkthrough: A cutter is a sailing vessel in the surface, but here it is a chopping tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something resembling a small axe, the hand tool used for chopping wood.

clue.text: Hollowed out part included reproductive cells in recession

indicators.note: recession is going backwards, so the cells word is read right to left

blocks.note: INC is the abbreviation for included
ova are egg cells

explanation.surface: An economic report: the reproductive sector caught up in a downturn.
explanation.definitionFit: In engraving, this Italian term names the part of a design cut into the surface, as in intaglio.

clue.text: What has frame for face set up with use of computers?

definitions.text: What has frame for face set up with use of computers?

blocks.note: E stands for electronic, as in email
to fit someone up is slang for to frame them

explanation.surface: A riddle about a frame for a face, built up with computers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the thing: a suspect's face put together on a computer, which might well frame someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Police use this computer-built likeness of a suspect, assembled from witness descriptions of facial features.

clue.text: Defame officer commanding former member of arcana

blocks.note: to tar someone is to blacken their name
OC is the abbreviation for officer commanding

explanation.surface: Slandering a commanding officer who once belonged to a secret society.
explanation.walkthrough: The arcana are the two sets of cards in a tarot pack.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old spelling of tarot, the card pack divided into major and minor arcana.

clue.text: Whenever close friend returned, hit deck and celebrated riotously

indicators.note: returned means coming back, so the pair is read backwards
something hit is knocked about, so the letters of the deck word are scrambled

blocks.note: if can mean whenever, as in if it rains we stay in
fam is slang for a close friend
taken as written

explanation.surface: Every time a mate came home, someone flattened the deck and partied wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb comes from the wild London street celebrations at the relief of Mafeking in the Boer War, 1900.
explanation.definitionFit: To maffick is to rejoice with boisterous public celebration, as crowds did at Mafeking's relief.

clue.text: King is out of black-tie role, entertaining classy star

indicators.note: the king letter leaves the black-tie word
to entertain is to host, so the role word holds the class letter

blocks.note: black-tie dress is formal
R is the abbreviation for rex, king
wearing many hats means having many roles
U means upper-class

explanation.surface: A king abandons a formal-dress part, hosting a stylish celebrity instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Star looks like the celebrity in the surface but is a real star in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the brightest point of light in the constellation Piscis Austrinus, the Southern Fish.

clue.text: Faddish toy from Japan — not magot but samurai sword

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the named letters from the toy word

blocks.note: the handheld digital pet craze of the 1990s
a magot is a small grotesque Japanese figurine

explanation.surface: Not a little figurine but a warrior's blade from Japan, beside a craze toy.
explanation.definitionFit: This long curved blade was worn edge-down by Japanese warriors before the katana became standard.
